Process: Baker's yeast (Saccharomyces cerevisiae) grown in a fed-batch bioreactor. Biomass concentration x1 and substrate (glucose) concentration x2 are measured every hour, in g/L. The operator sets the dilution rate u1 (1/h) and the substrate concentration in the feed u2 (g/L), both held constant between switches. Three experiments of 20 h with different starting biomass and input profiles. Measurement error is about 5% of the reading plus 0.01 g/L. The growth kinetics are unknown: find the rate law that explains the data.

Fitted candidates (all on the same data, 126 readings):

answer.feedback: C40 (Andrews inhibition kinetics) fits within the measurement noise, and all five parameters are estimated precisely (t-values above 1). It has Akaike weight 1.000, so it is clearly preferred among the fitted candidates. The fit was reached from only 2 of 4 starting points; this suggests some optimization sensitivity, so it would be prudent to verify the optimum with additional starts.
answer.reasoning: C40 is the only candidate that fits within the 95% chi-square limit and has every parameter estimated precisely. The other candidates show substantial lack of fit. The local-optimum warning is a caveat, not a reason to reject the qualifying fit.
